claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me the **name(s) of the child or children** you're inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. I'd like to know if I'm eligible for Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that context! So I'm assessing eligibility for your son **Alex**.

To help determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me: **What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 17 years old. He turned 17 earlier this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So Alex is 17 years old and turned 17 earlier this year.

Next, I need to ask: **Is Alex still in full-time education or an approved training course?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he actually left school recently, but he's just signed up with the careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex has left school and is now registered with the careers service.

I need to ask: **Is Alex currently registered as unemployed with the Jobcentre?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about the Jobcentre specifically, but he's registered with the careers service trying to work out his next steps.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that clarification. Let me ask a bit more specifically: **Has Alex registered as unemployed with the Jobcentre Plus, or is he claiming any benefits such as Universal Credit or Jobseeker's Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not claiming any benefits or registered with the Jobcentre. He's just working with the careers service at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one more important question:

**Is Alex a British citizen or do you know his immigration status?** (For example, is he a British citizen, or does he have settled status, a visa, or another immigration status in the UK?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's a British citizen. We both live here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the situation:
- Alex is 17 years old (turned 17 earlier this year)
- He has left school
- He is registered with the careers service but not in full-time education or approved training
- He is not registered with the Jobcentre or claiming any benefits
- He is a British citizen living in the UK

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, unfortunately you would **not be eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

Child Benefit can be paid for young people between 16 and 19 only if they are in full-time education or an approved training course. Since Alex has left school and is not in full-time education or an approved training course (he's simply registered with the careers service), he no longer meets the eligibility criteria.

Additionally, the fact that he's not registered as unemployed with the Jobcentre means he doesn't qualify under the alternative provisions that exist for 16-19 year-olds not in education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'm sorry to inform you that you're not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex at this time. However, if Alex does register with the Jobcentre as unemployed, or if he enrolls in full-time education or an approved training course, he may become eligible again. You might want to encourage him to explore those options with the careers service.

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old and no longer in full-time education or an approved training course, having recently left school. He is registered with the careers service but this does not constitute full-time education or approved training. He is also not registered as unemployed with the Jobcentre. Child Benefit for 16-19 year-olds requires either full-time education/approved training, or registration as unemployed with the Jobcentre. Since Alex meets neither of these conditions, he is not eligible for Child Benefit.
